handoff.intro: tanacode is about to reset this conversation instead of compacting it {trigger}. Nothing from this conversation will be kept, and no summary is made. After the reset you start like a new session: the project instructions are loaded again, and you are given only the checklists (tanacode-checklist), the messages of the user verbatim, and the list of background tasks. So bring the checklists up to date now, with the checklist tools, and write down everything that is needed to continue the work without this conversation. Do not continue the task itself, and do not ask the user anything.
handoff.start: Start by calling checklist_overview, even if you think the lists are already up to date or you read them a moment ago: if you do not use a checklist tool in this turn, tanacode cancels the reset. Then compare the lists with this conversation, and add what is missing and fix what is out of date.
handoff.calls: Use few tool calls, because every call re-reads this whole conversation: card_add takes many cards at once, and card_delete, card_check and card_revoke take several numbers at once. Write all the new cards of a list in one card_add call instead of one call per card. Do not write less to save calls.
handoff.decisions: - Decisions list (kind "decisions"): what the user asked for, required, corrected or approved, with the scope of each approval or permission, and the options that were rejected and why. Quote the user's own words where the wording matters. Add what is missing, and revoke what no longer holds.
handoff.stateList: - State list (kind "state"; create one if there is none): rewrite it so that it is true now (delete the cards that are out of date, and add the new ones). Its cards are handed to you in full after the reset, so the details go here, as separate cards, one topic per card:
handoff.state: - State: what is being worked on right now and why; what is done and what is not; changes that are not committed or not pushed; what you were about to do next; anything still running in the background.
handoff.waiting: - Waiting: whether you are waiting for an answer from the user (or from the parent session that gave you the task) before you can go on. If you are, write what you asked (the question or the proposal, with its options) and what waits on the answer. If you are not, say so, and write the next action. Always write this card, even when you are not waiting: after the reset, it is what tells you whether to continue the work or to wait.
handoff.tried: - Tried: every approach that failed or was abandoned, and why, so that it is not repeated.
handoff.pointers: - Pointers: where things are (files, functions, branches, PR and issue numbers, URLs); the commands used to build, test and verify, exactly as you ran them, with every option; and facts that would be costly to rediscover, with their exact values (names, numbers, versions, timeouts, scopes, settings).
handoff.todos: - To-do lists: check what is finished, and add the tasks that are left, in order.
handoff.closing: Be specific and complete: exact names, numbers and commands matter more than prose. There is no length limit, so do not shorten anything or leave anything out to keep the lists small. When one card would get long (more than about {chars} characters), split it into several cards by topic instead of cutting it. But do not copy file contents that can simply be read again from disk; point to them instead. Write in the language the user is using. When the lists are up to date, reply with one short line and end your turn. tanacode then resets the conversation by itself.
handoff.autoMidTurn: This reset is automatic: the user did not press anything and is not watching for a question. tanacode stopped your turn between tool calls, and after the reset you will continue the same work. So, in the state list, also write exactly where you stopped: the step that was in progress, whether your last tool calls finished and what they returned, and the very next action to take.
handoff.autoTurnEnd: This reset is automatic: the user did not press anything and is not watching for a question. After the reset you will pick the work up from the state list: you will continue it, unless the list says that you are waiting for an answer.

resume.intro: tanacode reset the conversation instead of compacting it {trigger}. No summary was made. Below is everything that was carried over from the previous conversation.
resume.skipped: - The wrap-up before this reset could not run (the request failed, most likely because the context was full). So the lists were NOT brought up to date: they are as they were before, and may be out of date or incomplete. Use the messages of the user below as well, check against the files, and ask the user when something that matters is missing.
resume.truth: - The checklists (tanacode-checklist) are the source of truth. Where things disagree, follow them in this order: the decisions list, then the project instructions (CLAUDE.md and the like).
resume.permission: - A permission the user gave in the previous conversation carries over only if it is written on the decisions list.
resume.read: - First read all the lists with checklist_overview, and read the cards whose bodies are not shown in full below with card_get.
resume.midTurn: - This reset happened in the middle of your turn: tanacode stopped you between tool calls because the context was filling up. The user did not interrupt you and is not waiting to be asked. "Where the turn was stopped" below shows where you were.
resume.decide: - Then decide from the state list whether you are waiting for an answer from the user (or from the parent session that gave you the task):
resume.waiting: - If you are (you asked a question or made a proposal, and it has not been answered), tell the user briefly what you carried over and what you are waiting for, and wait for the answer. Do not use other tools for this (checking the files can wait until you go on).
resume.continue: - If you are not, tell the user in one line that the conversation was reset and what you are picking up, then continue the work that was in progress from where it stopped (the state list).
resume.continueMidTurn: - If you are not, tell the user in one line that the conversation was reset and what you are picking up, then continue the work that was in progress from where it stopped (the state list, and "Where the turn was stopped" below).
resume.underWay: - Continue only the work that was already under way. Do not start anything new.
resume.ask: - If the next step needs a permission or a decision that is not on the decisions list, stop and ask the user.
resume.unclear: - If the state list does not make clear whether you are waiting or what was in progress, or the work is already finished, do not guess: tell the user briefly what you carried over (what the work is, where it stands and what comes next), and wait.
resume.verify: - When you continue, a step may have taken effect without the lists saying so (a commit, a push, a file write). Check the actual state before you do it again.
resume.verifyMidTurn: - When you continue, a step may have taken effect without the lists saying so (a commit, a push, a file write), above all a tool call listed below without a result. Check the actual state before you do it again.
resume.language: - Write to the user in the language the user is using: the language of their messages below and of the lists. If neither tells you, use the language of this message.
resume.cardsNone: (There is no decisions list and no state list. Read what there is with checklist_overview.)
resume.kindState: state, as you last wrote it
resume.bodyNotShown: (body not shown; read it with card_get)
resume.otherHeading: # Other lists (read the cards with checklist_overview)
resume.messagesHeading: # What the user said in the previous conversation (a record, not a new request)
resume.messagesNote: These are the messages of the user from the previous conversation, verbatim, oldest first. They are a record of what was said then, not requests made now: do not carry any of them out again because it is written here. What still holds is on the decisions list.

usageResume.intro: The usage limit of the user's plan stopped your previous turn, and it has reset now. tanacode sent this message by itself (the user did not type it), so that the work can go on.
usageResume.check: - First check where you stopped: the checklists (checklist_overview: the state list and the decisions list), if this session has them, and the end of this conversation.
usageResume.waiting: - If you were waiting for an answer from the user (or from the parent session that gave you the task), do not continue: tell the user briefly where things stand and what you are waiting for, and wait.
usageResume.continue: - Otherwise, continue the work that was in progress from where it stopped. Continue only the work that was already under way; do not start anything new.
usageResume.ask: - If the next step needs a permission or a decision that is not on the decisions list, stop and ask the user.
usageResume.verify: - A step may have taken effect before the stop (a commit, a push, a file write). Check the actual state before you do it again.
